questions.question: Absolute figures like R10 500 carry no verdict because:
options: A figure only gains meaning against a BASE — magnificent for a pavement stall, a disaster for a supermarket chain
Rand amounts change value every day

questions.question: Every profitability percentage asks:
options: How quickly is the stock turning over?
Out of every hundred rand of SALES, how many rand ended up as this?
How much sits in the bank account?
How old are the debtors' accounts?

questions.question: Because the formula summary supplies every formula, the skills being tested are:
options: SELECTION of the right formula, correct SUBSTITUTION, and INTERPRETATION

questions.question: The commonest calculation error in this topic is:
options: Feeding the WRONG FIGURE into a right formula — operating profit where net belongs, cost of sales where sales belongs

questions.question: Gross profit on SALES for Zanele's year is:
options: 20 000 / 60 000 × 100 = 33,3% — thirty-three rand thirty of margin from every hundred over the counter

questions.question: Gross profit on COST OF SALES computes to 50%, which is recognisable as:
options: THE MARK-UP — the pricing policy of 50% on cost, confirmed by actual trading
The interest rate on the loan

questions.question: The two gross percentages are:
options: The SAME profit read from the two ends of the counter — mark-up applied on cost, margin received on sales

questions.question: Achieved mark-up 44% against a policy of 50% signals:
options: The policy must be dropped to 44%
A recording error and nothing else
A FINDING — markdowns, stock lost after costing, recording errors or theft; the gap sizes the leak

subtopics.title: The Operating Family and Net Profit on Sales

questions.question: Operating expenses on sales is:
A RISING expense percentage across years means:
options: Expenses are growing FASTER than sales — the operating leak; the itemised list shows which line swells
The loan has become too large

questions.question: The distance between operating profit (20%) and net profit (17,5%) isolates:
options: The FINANCING bite — the loan's interest as a share of every hundred rand of sales

questions.question: The dashboard read in one glance:
options: Mark-up 50 achieved; margin 33,3; expenses 25,3; operations keep 20; owner keeps 17,5 — the earning story in portable proportions

questions.question: The three comparison bases are:
options: LAST YEAR (trend), the POLICY (control check), a SIMILAR BUSINESS (competitive check)
The bank, the auditor and the landlord

questions.question: The comment's four-move anatomy is:
options: STATE the figure with its comparison; JUDGE favourable/unfavourable; EXPLAIN the likely cause from the scenario; RECOMMEND one action
Restate the number four different ways

questions.question: "It went down" as a complete answer earns:
options: Only the first quarter of the marks — the STATE move without judge, explain or recommend

questions.question: Respecting what each percentage CAN say means:
options: Using every percentage in every answer
Gross percentages speak of pricing and stock control, the expense percentage of cost management — diagnose from the right gauge

questions.question: Following one hundred-rand note through Zanele's year gives:
options: R66,70 replaces the goods, R33,30 is margin, about R25,30 runs the shop, R17,50 remains as the owner's keep
R50 to stock, R50 to the owner
R30 to tax, R70 to wages

questions.question: Percentages "travel" and rand totals do not because:
options: Percentages are always the larger numbers
Per-hundred proportions can stand next to any year and any business; totals are trapped in their own year

questions.question: The five official percentages are:
options: The checkpoint names along the hundred-rand note's journey

subtopics.title: The Health Check at the Clinic

questions.question: "Temperature thirty-seven — fine or fever?" teaches that:
options: A vital sign means nothing until COMPARED — against the normal range or your own last visit
Every percentage has one healthy value

questions.question: Margin fine but the owner's keep thin points to:
options: The RUNNING COSTS — some expense line is swelling; the problem is not pricing

questions.question: Margin down but expenses steady points to:
options: An UPSTREAM leak — markdowns, missing stock, prices slipping

questions.question: The percentages "treat nothing" but:
options: They tell you WHICH ORGAN to examine, and catch sickness while it is still curable

questions.question: The four-line recipe in home language is:
options: WHAT happened; SO what (verdict); WHY (from the story); NOW WHAT (action)

questions.question: Line three's WHY must come from:
options: THE SCENARIO — supplied clues like a clearance sale or a burglary; analysis is detective work with given evidence

questions.question: Asked about pricing, the right gauges are:
options: The GROSS percentages — margin on sales and mark-up on cost

questions.question: The interpretation error markers meet most often is:
options: Comparing against two bases at once
Answering from the WRONG GAUGE — a percentage that cannot speak to the question asked
